document_status: DRAFT / PRIMARY-SOURCE CHECK COMPLETE / NOVELTY AND SPECIALIST REVIEW OPEN / RING 4 / NOT LICENSED / HELD
policy: Each source supports only its stated use_scope. Prior causal-abstraction theory does not validate the Project Coherence specialization, its proposed metrics, any empirical CAS/TKS claim, safety, product fitness, novelty, canon admission, licensing, or disclosure.

entries.authors: Paul K. Rubenstein, Sebastian Weichwald, Stephan Bongers, Joris M. Mooij, Dominik Janzing, Moritz Grosse-Wentrup, and Bernhard Schölkopf
entries.title: Causal Consistency of Structural Equation Models
entries.venue: Proceedings of the 33rd Conference on Uncertainty in Artificial Intelligence
entries.use_scope: Exact transformations between structural-equation models and the requirement that levels agree on intervention effects.
entries.boundary: Does not establish an exact or approximate transformation for CAS/TKS or identify a map from observational data.

entries.authors: Sander Beckers and Joseph Y. Halpern
entries.title: Abstracting Causal Models
entries.venue: Proceedings of the AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence 33(01), 2678-2685
entries.use_scope: Exact, uniform, strong, and state-map-induced causal abstraction distinctions; intervention maps are load-bearing.
entries.boundary: Does not supply a Project Coherence state map, intervention map, experiment, or empirical result.

entries.authors: Sander Beckers, Frederick Eberhardt, and Joseph Y. Halpern
entries.title: Approximate Causal Abstractions
entries.venue: Proceedings of the 35th Uncertainty in Artificial Intelligence Conference, PMLR 115:606-615
entries.use_scope: Approximate abstraction between low- and high-level causal models using application-dependent distances across interventions and contexts, including probabilistic extensions.
entries.boundary: Paper 5's kernel profile, non-vacuity gate, and proposed estimands are a new specialization and remain unvalidated.

entries.authors: Eigil F. Rischel and Sebastian Weichwald
entries.title: Compositional abstraction error and a category of causal models
entries.venue: Proceedings of the 37th Conference on Uncertainty in Artificial Intelligence, PMLR 161:1013-1023
entries.use_scope: Finite interventional causal models, abstraction transformations, and subadditive compositional error.
entries.boundary: The source's exact category and Jensen-Shannon construction are not silently identified with Paper 5's total-variation kernel profile.

entries.authors: Atticus Geiger, Hanson Lu, Thomas Icard, and Christopher Potts
entries.title: Causal Abstractions of Neural Networks
entries.venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 34
entries.use_scope: Alignment of neural representations with high-level causal variables and experimental testing through interchange interventions.
entries.boundary: The method and its reported task results do not validate a CAS/TKS alignment, semantic interpretation, safety measure, or product claim.

entries.authors: Riccardo Massidda, Atticus Geiger, Thomas Icard, and Davide Bacciu
entries.title: Causal Abstraction with Soft Interventions
entries.venue: Proceedings of the Second Conference on Causal Learning and Reasoning, PMLR 213:68-87
entries.use_scope: Extension of causal abstraction to soft interventions and conditions for an explicit intervention map.
entries.boundary: Paper 5 does not yet define or verify a CAS/TKS soft-intervention map.

entries.authors: Bernhard Schölkopf, Francesco Locatello, Stefan Bauer, Nan Rosemary Ke, Nal Kalchbrenner, Anirudh Goyal, and Yoshua Bengio
entries.title: Toward Causal Representation Learning
entries.use_scope: Causal representation learning as discovery of high-level causal variables from low-level observations and its distinction from standard representation learning.
entries.boundary: A learned representation is not automatically a verified approximate causal abstraction.

entries.authors: Kartik Ahuja, Jason Hartford, and Yoshua Bengio
entries.title: Interventional Causal Representation Learning
entries.venue: Proceedings of the 40th International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 202:372-407
entries.use_scope: An example of causal-representation identifiability under explicit intervention assumptions.
entries.boundary: Its assumptions and identifiability results do not automatically hold for neural activation interventions or CAS/TKS variables.

entries.title: A synthetic approach to Markov kernels, conditional independence and theorems on sufficient statistics
entries.use_scope: Markov kernels as stochastic morphisms and their composition.
entries.boundary: A Markov kernel or Markov category does not carry causal intervention semantics by default.

entries.title: Causal diagrams for empirical research
entries.use_scope: Graphical causal assumptions, interventions, and the distinction between identified and non-identified causal queries from nonexperimental data.
entries.boundary: A causal diagram identifies an effect only under its stated graphical and substantive assumptions; Paper 5 has not registered such a diagram for CAS/TKS.

entries.title: Characterization and Greedy Learning of Interventional Markov Equivalence Classes of Directed Acyclic Graphs
entries.use_scope: Observational Markov equivalence and the finer distinctions enabled by interventional data.
entries.boundary: Does not imply that any particular Project Coherence intervention set is sufficient for identification.

entries.title: On Multi-Cause Approaches to Causal Inference with Unobserved Counfounding: Two Cautionary Failure Cases and A Promising Alternative
entries.venue: Proceedings of the 22nd International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Statistics, PMLR 89:3478-3486
entries.use_scope: Analytical counterexamples and non-identification under unobserved confounding in multi-cause observational inference.
entries.boundary: The paper's specific multi-cause setting is not identical to Paper 5; it supports the general need for explicit identification assumptions.

entries.authors: Francesco Locatello, Stefan Bauer, Mario Lucic, Gunnar Rätsch, Sylvain Gelly, Bernhard Schölkopf, and Olivier Bachem
entries.title: Challenging Common Assumptions in the Unsupervised Learning of Disentangled Representations
entries.venue: Proceedings of the 36th International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 97:4114-4124
entries.use_scope: Non-identifiability of unsupervised disentanglement without inductive biases and supervision in the paper's setting.
entries.boundary: Does not prove non-identifiability for every causal representation-learning design or every intervention-rich setting.

entries.authors: Marc Lipsitch, Eric Tchetgen Tchetgen, and Ted Cohen
entries.title: Negative Controls: A Tool for Detecting Confounding and Bias in Observational Studies
entries.use_scope: Negative-control design as a method for detecting some forms of confounding and bias.
entries.boundary: Passing negative controls does not prove absence of all confounding, bias, or execution error.

entries.authors: Paul R. Rosenbaum and Donald B. Rubin
entries.title: The central role of the propensity score in observational studies for causal effects
entries.use_scope: Strong ignorability and balancing-score foundations for observational causal-effect estimation.
entries.boundary: Propensity adjustment does not repair unmeasured confounding or create an intervention map between causal models.

entries.authors: Miguel A. Hernán and James M. Robins
entries.title: Causal Inference: What If
entries.use_scope: Consistency, exchangeability, positivity, causal estimands, and design/analysis boundaries for causal inference.
entries.boundary: Standard assumptions must be justified for each Paper 5 target; the book does not validate any Project Coherence design.

entries.title: Designing and Interpreting Probes with Control Tasks
entries.use_scope: Control-task and selectivity methodology for representation probes.
entries.boundary: Probe selectivity does not establish causal abstraction, semantic correctness, safety, or product validity.

novelty_boundary: Exact and approximate causal abstraction, categorical abstraction error, neural interchange interventions, soft interventions, causal representation learning, causal identification, negative controls, and probe controls all have substantial prior literature. The Project Coherence combination remains novelty-unassessed and unreviewed.
